- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion bias.
- Model frequently overestimates 30-day mean by 2–8% when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward bias of 3–5% to 30d forecast average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model tends to misalign horizon; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is below 75% of 30d mean, model often overestimates; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment negativity.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to anticipate mean reversion; add 1–3% downward bias after 10–15 days of upward momentum.
